plan: [ This is a private-values, second-price auction with rational opponents. The weakly dominant strategy is to bid my true value: it maximizes expected profit because if I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not mine. Any shading risks losing profitable wins; overbidding risks negative payoff if I accidentally beat someone with a higher value. With no usable history and only 1 round, there's no benefit to deviating or experimenting. Therefore, bid exactly my value of 22.0 in $0.1 increments. ]

[ In a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values and rational opponents, the dominant strategy is to bid my true value. This maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies. There is only 1 round, so no learning or signaling benefits from deviation. Bids are in $0.1 increments and ties are random; bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever the second-highest value is below mine and pay that second-highest bid, yielding nonnegative surplus. I will bid $15.0. ]

[ In a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values and rational opponents, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Overbidding risks negative payoff if a rival’s value exceeds mine; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. With value $10 and no future rounds to influence, bid exactly 10 to maximize expected profit. ]
